project.name: hackprinceton (Leto)
project.description: A hackathon project for building energy analysis: a Python FastAPI backend (data layer for CoStar, Matterport, Vexcel, weather and tariffs; physics/solar/finance analysis; a LangGraph-based agent; legal drafting) with a React + Three.js frontend, coordinated by a GitHub-issue message board that lets teammates' coding agents hand off work. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Entry Point and Spec
tour.description: Leto is a building-energy retrofit consultant: pick a property and a budget, and it reads the building, simulates its energy use, and returns a funded retrofit plan with optional legal drafts. Everything starts at backend/server.py, a thin uvicorn entry that exposes the FastAPI app built by the factory in backend/agent/server/app.py, which wires run, document, search and property routes. specs/SPEC.md is the master product spec that the code cites throughout, so keep it open as your map.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's application-factory pattern (a create_app function returning the app) lets tests build fresh, independently configured app instances, while a module-level `app` object gives uvicorn a stable import target.

tour.title: The Shared Contract
tour.description: backend/schema.py is by far the most depended-upon file in the graph (fan-in 123): a Pydantic model set generated from SPEC.md section 9 that defines PropertyBundle, BuildingModel, Measure, Plan, RunResult and RunEvent. Every lane (data, analysis, agent, legal) speaks only these types, and frontend/src/lib/types.ts mirrors them in TypeScript for the browser. backend/config.py holds the non-secret settings, such as model ids and ask-rule limits, each cited back to the spec.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models give runtime validation plus static typing: data parsed into a model is guaranteed to match the declared schema, which makes a single generated file a safe contract between independently developed modules.

tour.title: Runs: Replay and Live
tour.description: The agent lane's 'run door' in backend/agent/api.py starts, streams, patches and documents runs in two modes: replay (golden fixtures) or live. LiveRun in live.py drives the agent on a background thread and event loop, and runtime.py maps agent stream chunks into RunEvents and persists the final RunResult from Step 2. analysis_run.py is a model-free mode that calls the analysis lane directly, which is useful for deterministic demos.

tour.title: The Auditor Agent
tour.description: graph.py builds a deepagents (LangGraph) auditor that orchestrates scout, surveyor, physicist and financier subagents, plus a counsel subagent for legal drafting. The agent never touches the analysis directly: tools.py wraps around 20 door functions that read large objects from run files. narrative.py enforces a no-arithmetic rule, checking every number in the agent's prose against computed results, and ask.py implements the ask rule that poses sensitivity questions to the user one at a time.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping the LLM away from arithmetic is a common agent-safety pattern: tools return computed numbers, and a post-check rejects any narrative number that does not trace back to a tool result.

tour.title: The Data Layer
tour.description: backend/data_layer/api.py is the data lane's single public door: it searches properties and assembles a PropertyBundle from three views of a building. costar.py reads the CoStar market record, matterport.py pulls interior scan geometry over GraphQL, and vexcel.py fetches aerial parcel and roof attributes. cache.py, the third most imported file, records a FetchRecord for every fetch so each fact carries provenance and can be replayed offline.

tour.title: Building Model and Vision
tour.description: backend/analysis/api.py is the analysis lane's facade (the widest fan-out in the backend): it turns the PropertyBundle from Step 5 into a BuildingModel, then runs the baseline, measures and plan. geometry/build.py converts Matterport rooms and wall graphs into thermal zones and envelope surfaces, vision/interior.py reads interior panoramas with a vision model, and registry.py merges CoStar, Vexcel, vision and vintage defaults into sourced assumptions.

tour.title: Climate and Solar Physics
tour.description: Physics starts with the sun and the weather. data_layer/external.py builds the ClimateSite from a typical-year weather file, physics/climate/weather.py parses hourly CSVs like the committed Los Angeles sample, and spa.py is a vectorised NumPy port of the NREL Solar Position Algorithm. pv/chain.py turns that irradiance into hourly PV output, following the formula ids in specs/physics/01-solar-pv.md.
tour.languageLesson: NumPy vectorisation evaluates a formula over all 8,760 hours as array operations instead of a Python loop, often 50-100x faster, which matters when every measure re-runs the simulation.

tour.title: Hourly Thermal Baseline
tour.description: zone/model.py runs an hourly simulation over the BuildingModel from Step 6 using the ISO 13790 5R1C thermal network in rc.py. systems/baseline.py converts those zone loads into HVAC, hot water, lighting and plug energy by end use, and calibration/calibrate.py tunes the model against twelve months of utility bills to ASHRAE Guideline 14 accuracy. specs/physics/02-thermal-systems.md documents every equation.

tour.title: Rooftop Solar Design
tour.description: Solar design reuses the aerial data from Step 5 and the PV chain from Step 7. roof/planes.py builds parametric roof planes from the Vexcel footprint and shape class, layout/layout.py packs panels onto them by yield per panel, and measures/pv/pv.py converts the finished SolarDesign into bill savings and export value so it can compete with other measures.

tour.title: The Measure Engine
tour.description: Retrofit measures are plug-ins: engine.py keeps a registry, checks each measure's applicability (home or office flow, owner or tenant role, consent) and re-runs the baseline from Step 8 with the change applied. catalogue.py lists the SPEC 6.2 measure library as data, attic.py and heat_pump.py show typical check/change/describe plug-ins, and costs.py prices each measure from sourced cost tables.
tour.languageLesson: A plug-in registry maps measure ids to small functions with a common signature (check, change, describe), so adding a measure means writing one module without editing the engine.

tour.title: Budget Plan and Finance
tour.description: plan.py is where the user's budget comes in: it orders the measures from Step 10 operations-first, then load reduction, equipment and solar, and selects what fits. economics.py computes NPV, SIR and payback, cpace.py models C-PACE financing for measures that exceed the budget, value.py estimates property value uplift, and sensitivity.py finds which assumptions move the plan most, which feeds the ask rule from Step 4.

tour.title: Golden Example Runs
tour.description: specs/examples holds golden fixtures for a house and two offices, one in Los Angeles and one in Houston. run_result.json is a complete RunResult and run_events.json is the event stream the frontend replays. analysis_stub.py replays these folders behind the same signatures as the real analysis API, so the agent and frontend lanes could be built in parallel before the physics existed.

tour.title: Legal Drafting
tour.description: Once a plan exists, the legal lane drafts the paperwork. legal/api.py lists templates by state and segment, engine.py fills {{placeholders}} in Markdown templates such as the California residential retrofit contract, and checks.py runs one statutory predicate per California rule over the draft. specs/legal.md defines the templates, the clause library and the Texas and C-PACE variants.

tour.title: The React Frontend
tour.description: main.tsx mounts App.tsx, the root shell that handles property search, live SSE runs or saved replays, and screen navigation. lib/api.ts is the typed client for the routes from Step 1, Plan.tsx renders the budget plan from Step 11 with savings ranges and sources, and HouseViewer.tsx wraps a Three.js scene that shows the building in exterior, cutaway and exploded modes.
tour.languageLesson: Server-Sent Events (EventSource) give a one-way stream from server to browser over plain HTTP. They suit agent progress streams where the client only listens, and they reconnect automatically.

tour.title: Team Workflow and CI
tour.description: Leto was built by several humans with coding agents working in parallel lanes. AGENTS.md sets the rules (a pinned GitHub message board, one writer per path, contract changes by agreement), README.md explains the board and the demo, and specs/workplan.md defines each lane's public door. The frontend.yml GitHub Actions workflow checks frontend compatibility on every push and pull request.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows declare `on` triggers (push, pull_request), then jobs made of sequential steps. Path filters can limit a workflow to changes under one directory, such as frontend/.
